supporting_observations.claim: The PowerShell process on WS-MSANTOS-01 was launched at 13:43:10 by ken.ito with the exact command to run the organization's documented workstation patch script, \\FILE-BLU-01\IT\Patch-Workstations.ps1.
Shortly beforehand, WS-MSANTOS-01 recorded a network logon for ken.ito from WS-KITO-01; the PowerShell process used the same ken.ito logon ID.

The patch script launched wusa.exe to install a Windows update, and the workstation connected to download.windowsupdate.com with a Windows Update Agent user agent. This is consistent with the documented patching activity.
The logged PowerShell launch was at 13:43, not around 13:40; the records provided do not show a PowerShell process at the reported time.

known_telemetry_limitations: The process records provide the PowerShell command line but not the patch script's contents or a hash that would independently verify the script executed.
The available records do not establish what Mia saw on screen or the exact time the reported window appeared; the logged PowerShell process starts at 13:43:10 (T194-00178, T194-00179).
claims_not_established: The records do not establish that the brief window Mia reported around 13:40 was the PowerShell process logged at 13:43.
The records do not independently verify the contents of \\FILE-BLU-01\IT\Patch-Workstations.ps1.
unrelated_findings: Separate review recommended: WS-MSANTOS-01 obtained Kerberos tickets for ruth.moss, followed by network logons to WS-RMOSS-01 from WS-MSANTOS-01; the records also show certificate preauthentication for ruth.moss from that workstation. This is not evidence that the alerted PowerShell activity was malicious. (T194-00161, T194-00162, T194-00165, T194-00172, T194-00173, T194-00175)

Separate review recommended: Mia's browser accessed drive.google.com, a cloud-storage service not listed as approved in the supplied inventory. The records show page and related resource requests, but do not establish file upload or download. (T194-00327, T194-00328, T194-00333, T194-00338)
